recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-3059 unless Pharmacy later requests a broader example or terminology update beyond the original one-fill quantity clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-3059 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request for MedicationPrescription.quantity, applied for DSTU1, asking that the quantity definition make clear it is the amount dispensed at one time rather than the total amount authorized across repeats.
initial_application: No explicit FHIR-3059-tagged source commit was found. Git history shows the original MedicationPrescription source introduced the dispense quantity definition without the one-fill clarification in 6bf66c167ce30cc7fe9398849a898c25880cdb92, then abce09d8c1edffa07e8bd6fbdf60eaa097da3d91 changed MedicationPrescription.dispense.quantity to "The amount that is to be dispensed for one fill."
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists medicationrequest as an active resource and records that MedicationPrescription became MedicationRequest. The current combined branch has MedicationRequest.dispenseRequest.quantity short text "Amount of medication to supply per dispense" and definition "The amount that is to be dispensed for one fill." Related FHIR-8143 clarified numberOfRepeatsAllowed and is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active FHIR core source already preserves the requested semantic clarification at MedicationRequest.dispenseRequest.quantity, so another source edit would be redundant.

related_jiras.note: Clarified that numberOfRepeatsAllowed counts additional fills and not the original dispense, supporting the quantity-versus-total-authorized interpretation; it is already represented on the combined branch and was not republished.
